name: TCI Islander Status -- Spouse of an Islander

qualifying_event.description: The spouse of a TCI Islander (who did not themselves acquire status through marriage) may apply for TCI Islander status after 10 years of cohabitation and 2 years of TCI residence.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Marriage certificate; proof of 10 years' cohabitation; proof of 2 years' TCI residence; spouse's proof of TCI status acquired other than by marriage.

requirements.blocker_text: The Islander spouse must not have acquired their own TCI status through marriage (i.e. the spouse must hold status by birth, descent, adoption, or grant).
Requires 10 years of cohabitation with the Islander spouse immediately preceding the application.
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 10 years of cohabitation with the Islander spouse.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires 2 years of residence in TCI immediately preceding the application.

sources.title: Government of the Turks and Caicos Islands -- TCI Islander Status: spouse-of-Islander grant route (10-year cohabitation, 2-year residence, applicable year-round unlike the annual non-marriage application window), fee schedule, Turks and Caicos Islander Status Commission review

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of the Turks and Caicos Islands' initial build. Notable rule confirmed on the source page: marriage-based applications may be submitted at any time once the qualifying period is met, unlike all other (non-marriage) TCI Status grant applications, which are restricted to a June 1 - September 30 annual window each year -- flagged prominently since it materially affects timing for anyone using this route versus tc_islander_status_grant.json. Also notable: the spouse's OWN status must not itself have been acquired through marriage -- i.e. this route cannot be chained (a spouse who became an Islander via marriage cannot pass status on to a subsequent spouse the same way). Applications are reviewed by the Turks and Caicos Islander Status Commission against public-interest and good-character criteria in addition to the tenure requirements.
